description: Trusted client-IP derivation (#158 / #174). ONE golden, TWO stacks: TS `clientIpFrom` (packages/api/src/lib/client-ip.ts, asserted by tests/governance/audit-ip-derivation.test.ts) and C# `Tims.Domain.Http.ClientIp.From` (asserted by Tims.UnitTests/Http/ClientIpFixtureTests.cs). The rule: NEVER the client-controlled left-most x-forwarded-for hop; prefer x-real-ip (platform-edge, unspoofable), else the LAST xff hop. `expected: null` means no trusted address could be derived. A behaviour change edits this file once and must face both suites.

cases.name: takes the LAST hop, never the attacker-chosen first
many hops still resolves to the last
a blank x-real-ip falls through rather than winning as empty
a trailing comma does not produce an empty last hop
x-real-ip is trimmed when it does win
neither header present yields no address
an all-separator x-forwarded-for yields no address, not an empty string
IPv6 loopback (what local dev writes) survives verbatim
